title: Predicting NBA All-Star Selection from Player Performance and Team Record
text: Data provenance. player- team-level CSVs style Basketball-Reference season tables. Raw files live data/NBA Stats Data/ (22 CSVs, read within vignette; shipped package). relevant tables analysis : Player Per Game.csv — one row per player per team-stint per season, per-game stats -Star Selections.csv — one row per -Star selected per season Player Season Info.csv — biographical details per player-season Team Summaries.csv — one row per team per season (wins, arena, attendance) season variable coded year season ends (e.g. 1980 = 1979–80). Per proposal, use completed seasons — 1980 2026. 2027 season (2026–27) progress: per-game stats partial 2027 -Star game played yet, rows falsely labeled non-selections. subtlety: players traded mid-season appear multiple rows per-game file (one per team-stint) — season-total rows. attach -Star outcome (player_id, season) team record (team, season) (team abbreviations like BOS, LAL). season-level exposures traded player keep stint games played (slice_max(g)); alternative — games-weighted average per-game stats across stints — noted Limitations.  far every row player-season. next looks aggregate one row per player: total career -Star selections, along career scoring, rebounding assist averages. (weights seasons equally — career twenty seasons counts two-season career.) 1. many times player selected? Selection concentrated: -Stars appear twice, thin tail perennial selections (Kareem Abdul-Jabbar leads era 22).  2. Career scoring / rebounding / assist averages vs. number selections, primary position. Hover point see player. Jitter added vertically overlapping points readable; y-variable count, static version plots overplot heavily. leaves us. analysis table dat one row per player-season per-game stats, binary -Star outcome, team wins, attendance proxies. Remaining decisions modeling: operationalize “fanbase size” (arena capacity CSVs — attend_g closest proxy), whether traded players’ stats weighted rather max-games. See proposal pre-specified confounder set.
code: ── Attaching core tidyverse packages ──────────────────────── tidyverse 2.0.0 ── ✔ dplyr     1.2.1     ✔ readr     2.2.0 ✔ forcats   1.0.1     ✔ stringr   1.6.0 ✔ ggplot2   4.0.4     ✔ tibble    3.3.1 ✔ lubridate 1.9.5     ✔ tidyr     1.3.2 ✔ purrr     1.2.2 ── Conflicts ────────────────────────────────────────── tidyverse_conflicts() ── ✖ dplyr::filter() masks stats::filter() ✖ dplyr::lag()    masks stats::lag() ℹ Use the conflicted package (<http://conflicted.r-lib.org/>) to force all conflicts to become errors # Per-game stats, completed seasons only player_seasons <- per_game |>   filter(season >= 1980, season <= 2026)  # The outcome: whether a (player_id, season) appears in the selections file. allstar_flag <- allstar |>   filter(season >= 1980, season <= 2026) |>   distinct(player_id, season) |>   mutate(all_star = TRUE)  # Team record + fanbase proxies, keyed to (team abbreviation, season). team_wins <- teamsum |>   filter(season >= 1980, season <= 2026) |>   group_by(abbreviation, season) |>   slice_max(w, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>   # defensive: one row per team-season   ungroup() |>   select(team_abbr = abbreviation, season,          team_wins = w, team_losses = l,          arena, attend, attend_g) star_ps <- player_seasons |>   left_join(allstar_flag, by = c("player_id", "season")) |>   mutate(all_star = !is.na(all_star)) dat <- star_ps |>   group_by(player_id, season) |>   slice_max(g, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>   ungroup() |>   left_join(team_wins, by = c("team" = "team_abbr", "season")) # Count of player-seasons at each scoring level, split by outcome. # Counts (not within-group densities) keep the ~19:1 imbalance visible: ggplot(dat, aes(pts_per_game, fill = all_star)) +   geom_histogram(position = "identity", alpha = 0.6, binwidth = 1) +   labs(x = "Points per game", y = "Number of player-seasons", fill = "All-Star") career <- dat |>   group_by(player_id, player) |>   summarise(     n_selections = sum(all_star, na.rm = TRUE),     pts_pg       = mean(pts_per_game, na.rm = TRUE),     trb_pg       = mean(trb_per_game, na.rm = TRUE),     ast_pg       = mean(ast_per_game, na.rm = TRUE),     # modal position across the career (hybrid "PF-C" strings would lose detail)     pos = {       nonmiss <- pos[!is.na(pos)]       if (length(nonmiss)) names(which.max(table(nonmiss))) else NA_character_     },     .groups = "drop"   ) |>   mutate(across(c(pts_pg, trb_pg, ast_pg), ~ round(.x, 2))) ggplot(career |> filter(n_selections > 0), aes(n_selections)) +   geom_histogram(binwidth = 1) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::breaks_width(2)) +   labs(x = "Career All-Star selections (1980–2026)",        y = "Number of distinct players",        title = "Career All-Star selections are highly skewed",        subtitle = "Only players selected at least once are shown") plotly_stats <- setNames(   c("pts_pg", "trb_pg", "ast_pg"),   c("Career points per game", "Career rebounds per game", "Career assists per game") )  widgets <- lapply(names(plotly_stats), function(lab) {   var <- plotly_stats[[lab]]   g <- ggplot(career |> filter(!is.na(pos)),               aes(x = .data[[var]], y = n_selections)) +     geom_point(aes(color = pos, text = player),                alpha = 0.7, size = 1.5, position = position_jitter(height = 0.15)) +     labs(x = lab, y = "Career All-Star selections", color = "Position")   plotly::ggplotly(g, tooltip = c("text", "x", "y", "color")) })  htmltools::tagList(lapply(widgets, htmltools::div))
